styleWhy: Coffee's story is geography: a belt of growing countries around the equator and the sea routes that carry the beans north, which a map shows at a glance.

copy.idea: Where the world's coffee comes from: the band of tropical countries that grow it, the few that dominate, and the routes that carry it to the cups of Europe and North America.
copy.hook: About 170 million bags of coffee are grown every year. Where?
copy.body:
Around 170 million 60-kilo bags of coffee are produced every year.

Almost all of it grows in a band around the equator, between the tropics: the coffee belt, more than 70 countries.

One country leads by far: Brazil grows about a third of the world's coffee.

Next come Vietnam, mostly robusta, then Colombia, Indonesia and Ethiopia.

Ethiopia is where arabica coffee began.

From the belt, the beans sail north: the European Union and the United States are the biggest importers.

Every cup, a long journey.

facts.text: World coffee production is about 170 million 60-kg bags a year.
facts.source: International Coffee Organization, Coffee Market Report (2023/24 crop year), https://www.ico.org

facts.text: Coffee is grown in more than 70 countries, almost all between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn (the 'coffee belt').
facts.source: National Coffee Association USA, 'Where Coffee Grows', https://www.ncausa.org

facts.text: Brazil is the largest producer, with about a third of world output (≈66 of ≈175 million bags ≈ 38%).
facts.source: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Coffee: World Markets and Trade (2024), https://www.fas.usda.gov

facts.text: The top five producers are Brazil, Vietnam, Colombia, Indonesia and Ethiopia; Vietnam grows mostly robusta.
facts.source: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Coffee: World Markets and Trade (2024), https://www.fas.usda.gov

facts.text: Arabica coffee originated in the highlands of Ethiopia.
The European Union and the United States are the largest coffee importers.
facts.source: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Coffee: World Markets and Trade (2024), https://www.fas.usda.gov

shots.title: 170 million bags
shots.show: The whole globe, dark navy oceans and slate land, turning slowly. Small coffee-bean pins pop up one after another around the equator while a big gold rolling counter at the top climbs to ≈170 million and lands with a bounce, the unit 'bags / year' beneath it.
shots.text: ≈170 million bags a year. From where?
shots.motion: Globe rotates; bean pins pop in with a small bounce in a ripple along the equator; counter rolls from 0 and bounces on 170,000,000.

shots.title: The coffee belt
shots.show: The globe unrolls into the flat world map. Two dashed lines draw on, labelled Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn; the band between them fills with a soft gold glow. Then the growing countries light leaf green one by one from the Americas to Africa to Asia, while a small counter beside the band ticks up to 70+.
shots.text: Grown in 70+ countries between the tropics
shots.motion: Globe-to-flat morph; tropic lines draw left to right; band fades in; country fills ripple west to east; counter ticks to 70+.
shots.source: National Coffee Association USA, 'Where Coffee Grows'

shots.title: Brazil leads
shots.show: Camera flies from the world into South America. Brazil fills a brighter leaf green and grows a gold pin with rank badge '1'. Beside it a big counter rolls to ≈1/3, and a split bar at the bottom (the world's coffee) splits: Brazil's third in green, the rest in dim slate.
shots.motion: Zoom and pan into Brazil; the fill pulses brighter; pin drops; counter rolls; split bar wipes and separates into its two shares.
shots.source: USDA FAS, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, 2024 (≈66 of ≈175M bags ≈ 38%)

shots.title: The top five
shots.show: Camera pulls back out to the coffee belt. Rank pins drop in turn with their badges: 2 Vietnam (labelled 'robusta'), 3 Colombia, 4 Indonesia, 5 Ethiopia, each country brightening to the same leaf green as Brazil, which keeps its '1' pin.
shots.motion: Camera glides east across the belt; each pin drops with a bounce as the camera passes; country names type on beside the pins.
shots.source: USDA FAS, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, 2024

shots.title: Where arabica began
shots.show: Camera flies into East Africa. Ethiopia's highlands glow warm gold inside its green fill; its '5' pin stays, and a small coffee-plant icon sprouts on the highlands with the label 'arabica'. Faint ripples spread from it across the map.
shots.motion: Zoom into the Horn of Africa; gold glow breathes; plant icon grows leaf by leaf; ripple rings expand outward.

shots.title: Routes north
shots.show: Camera pulls out to the full flat map with the belt and the five green producers. Coffee-orange arcs draw on from Brazil, Colombia, Vietnam, Indonesia and Ethiopia to two destinations that light cool blue: the European Union and the United States. Small bean dots run along every arc like a flow.
shots.text: Most sails north to Europe and the US
shots.motion: Arcs draw on one after another; destination fills fade in blue; bean dots stream continuously along the arcs; camera drifts slowly north.
shots.source: USDA FAS, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, 2024 (largest importers)

shots.title: End card
shots.show: The globe again, slowly turning, wrapped in the glowing orange routes from the previous shot, bean dots still flowing; the title 'Where does the world's coffee come from' settles above it.
shots.motion: Globe turns; arcs shimmer; bean dots keep running; title fades and settles.

recurring.name: World map with the coffee belt
recurring.design: Navy ocean, slate-grey land; the coffee belt is a soft gold band between two dashed tropic lines labelled at the left edge; growing countries in leaf green (meaning: where coffee grows), always the same green.

recurring.name: Rank pins
recurring.design: Gold teardrop pins with a white numeric badge 1–5 (Brazil 1, Vietnam 2, Colombia 3, Indonesia 4, Ethiopia 5), country name in white type to the right of the pin; once dropped they stay.

recurring.name: Trade routes
recurring.design: Coffee-orange arcs bowing north from each top-five producer to its destination, with small bean-shaped dots flowing along them; importing destinations (EU, US) fill cool blue (meaning: where coffee goes).
